title: Metal cap stamps accelerate Javanese batik
summary: Metal stamps called cap made it possible to apply wax designs more quickly in Javanese batik, alongside the hand-drawn canting technique.

citations.note: Supports the linked claims within the stated date and attribution limits.

claims.text: Metal stamps called cap made it possible to apply wax designs more quickly in Javanese batik, alongside the hand-drawn canting technique.
The gallery dates cap development to the mid-nineteenth century. 1850 is a rounded anchor, not an attested first invention.
Wax prevents dye from reaching selected areas of cloth. The National Gallery of Australia describes stamping as faster but less flexible than drawing wax designs.

review.corroboration: The NGA Batik glossary passage was inspected in its indexed copy after direct access failed. Searches did not establish an independent date; that limit is recorded.
